sentences.text: Admittedly, it is an undisputed fact that petitioners were riding in the motor cycle as on the date of alleged accident.
The said fact has been admitted by PW1 in his cross-examination also.
The petitioners contended that only on the part of negligence of offending Car driver the accident was occurred.
In this regard it is already held that accident was occurred due to rash and negligence of the offending Car driver.
Now the question before the court is whether triple riding in motor Cycle amounts to a contributory negligence for occurrence of accident?.
The triple riding or riding more than seating capacity in a motor cycle is an absolute violation of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act.
In the instant case admittedly the pillion riders were minors having age of 11 and 14 years respectively.
Now the question before the court is if two minors riding in a motor cycle as pillion riders amounts to violation of motor vehicles Act or not?.

The learned counsel for respondent argued that even if  SCCH-9 24 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 minors were riding as pillion riders with triple riding that amounts to violation of Motor Vehicle Act and attract contributory negligence. In this regard he has relied upon the following reported judgments:
 1) 2004 (1) KLJ 498 (P.S.Somaiah & anr V/s  The Director, Bangalore Dairy and Others), wherein it Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/
18  is observed that - If any rider of Motor cycle violates Sec.128 of M.V.Act moving in a triple riding then  contributory negligence to be considered and  compensation should be apportioned on the  apportionment of negligence.
 2) 2003 (2) TAC 103 (Managing Director, Tamil  Nadu State Transport Corporation (Coimbatore Dvn)
 Ltd., Coimbatore V/s Abdul Salam & Others), wherein  Hon'ble Madras High Court observed that riding the  motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a  negligence and contributory negligence be considered  while awarding the compensation in accident case.
 3) 2017 ACJ 418 (New India Assurance Co..,
 Ltd., V/s Hemanth & Others), wherein the Hon'ble  High Court of Karnataka observed that- in case of  triple riding there is a contributory negligence and  SCCH-9 25 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022  liability to be fixed on apportionment to the insurance  companies.
 4) The unreported judgment of Hon'ble High  Court of Karnataka in MFA No.5314/2009 (MV)
 between H.B. Hemakeshwarappa V/s Abdul Roop  Khan

 " 10.

sentences.text: We are concerned as to whether such action of  the individuals is permissible under law.
The motor
cycle and any other two wheelers are meant only for  two persons, the rider and a pillion rider.
If more  than two persons are travelling in a motor cycle or  any other two wheeler, undoubtedly such action of  the individual would become illegal and un  authorised.
It is an awful sight when we come across  three persons travelling in a motor cycle.
They are  sitting in such a cramped manner that the rider of  the motor cycle almost sitting on the petrol tank or at  the front edge of the seat.
When he was sitting in  such a position, naturally because of the restricted  movement of his legs, he cannot have the complete  control over the brake.
The movements of his hands  also so restricted.
When that be so, this court is of  the opinion that definitely the rider of the two wheeler  cannot have full control over the vehicle.

11. Apart from that, when three persons are  travelling in a motor cycle, two as pillion riders, any  unusual movement of the pillion riders would make  SCCH-9 27 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022  the rider of the motor cycle to loose his control over  the vehicle.
Even though such travelling of three  persons in a motor cycle is contrary to the statute

,
 still the enforcement wing do not care to take note of  the same and failed to take action against their illegal  action.
Virtually because of the failure on the part of  the enforcement wing, such travelling of three  persons in the two wheelers has become a regular  sight.
